proposed_fix.description: Verify socket/connection pressure on recommendationservice pods and, if confirmed, relieve it via a gated, reversible restart or scale-out.
steps: Inspect recommendationservice pods for socket counts (e.g. `kubectl exec <pod> -- ss -s`) and compare with the pre-incident baseline in E1.
Check whether the ListRecommendations request rate (E3, ~9.9k log lines) is elevated versus normal, and identify callers (e.g. frontend) driving it.
Check the node's conntrack usage (R1) on the nodes hosting recommendationservice, e.g. `conntrack -C` vs `nf_conntrack_max`, to see whether the node is also a bottleneck.
If socket exhaustion on the pods is confirmed, with approval scale recommendationservice replicas up by a small increment to spread connections.
If a single pod holds leaked or stuck sockets, with approval do a rolling restart of that deployment, one pod at a time, watching latency-50/90 and frontend-external_error.
Review client connection handling (connection reuse, gRPC channel pooling, keepalive/timeouts) for a longer-term fix.
preconditions: Confirm the recommendationservice_socket anomaly is still active and not a recovered transient.
Confirm spare cluster capacity exists before scaling.
Confirm a rolling restart will not take capacity below what current traffic needs.
Human on-call approves each change step.
proposed_fix.rollback: Scale replicas back to the original count; if a rollout caused problems, run `kubectl rollout undo deployment/recommendationservice`. The inspection steps are read-only and need no rollback.
